insider_note: Tanh⁻¹x and Tan⁻¹x look almost identical in writing — the ONLY difference is the h — so read the denominator's sign carefully before choosing which one to write: 1−x² takes the hyperbolic one, 1+x² the circular one.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Split into two standard integrals
steps.why: The integrand is already a sum of two separate standard forms — no algebra is needed beyond recognising each piece on sight.
common_mistakes: Trying to combine the two fractions into one over a common denominator first, which only complicates the working.
Missing that these are two DIFFERENT standard results, not the same formula applied twice.
steps.memory_tip: 1−x² in a denominator signals Tanh⁻¹; 1+x² signals Tan⁻¹ — two completely different standard results, spotted on sight.

steps.label: Apply both standard formulas for the final answer
steps.why: Both pieces are standard, memorised results with a=1, so no completing the square or substitution is needed — just quote the two formulas and add.
common_mistakes: Writing log|(1+x)/(1−x)| in place of Tanh⁻¹x — the equivalent log form is also correct, but mixing the two notations in one line is untidy.
Only one +c for the whole sum, which is correct, but forgetting it entirely.
steps.memory_tip: Two standard results, added — one h, one without — and a single +c at the very end.
